name: Tafamidis
route_note: oral capsule once daily (tafamidis meglumine 80 mg or free acid 61 mg)
originator: FoldRx Pharmaceuticals (from Jeffery Kelly's laboratory, Scripps Research)

discovery.by: Jeffery Kelly and colleagues, Scripps Research Institute
discovery.note: Structure-based design of small molecules that bind the thyroxine sites of the TTR tetramer; Pfizer acquired FoldRx in 2010.

tagline: First drug to stabilise transthyretin and treat ATTR cardiomyopathy
summary: Tafamidis binds and stabilises the transthyretin tetramer, preventing its dissociation into monomers that misfold into amyloid. It treats transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, both hereditary and wild-type, and in some countries hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.
mechanism: Transthyretin is a liver-made tetramer that carries thyroxine and retinol-binding protein. Dissociation of the tetramer is the rate-limiting step in amyloid formation; released monomers misfold and aggregate into fibrils deposited in heart and nerves.
Tafamidis binds the two thyroxine-binding sites with negative cooperativity, kinetically stabilising the native tetramer and slowing amyloidogenesis. It does not remove existing deposits.
uses: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (wild-type or hereditary) in adults
Hereditary transthyretin amyloid polyneuropathy, stage 1 (EU, Japan and other markets)

history.title: Acquisition
history.detail: Pfizer acquires FoldRx, developer of tafamidis.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU for early-stage hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.

history.title: FDA rejection
history.detail: The FDA declines approval for polyneuropathy, requesting more efficacy data.

history.title: ATTR-ACT
history.detail: Tafamidis reduces all-cause mortality and cardiovascular hospitalisation in ATTR cardiomyopathy.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US for ATTR cardiomyopathy as Vyndaqel and Vyndamax; its high list price draws criticism.

history.title: Competition
history.detail: The FDA approves acoramidis, another TTR stabiliser, for ATTR cardiomyopathy.

history.title: RNA silencer approved
history.detail: Vutrisiran becomes the first TTR silencer approved in the US for ATTR cardiomyopathy.

facts: Jeffery Kelly's work on tafamidis provided clinical proof that kinetic stabilisation of a protein can slow an amyloid disease.
It is one of Pfizer's largest-selling products.

references.title: Maurer MS et al. Tafamidis treatment for patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-ACT). N Engl J Med 2018
